5,000+ learning games, books, and videos for kids ages 2–8. Always 100% free, no ads, no subscriptions—just safe, joyful learning kids and parents love. Make screen time more meaningful with Khan Academy Kids—the award-winning, educational app for kids ages 2–8. Packed with fun, standards-aligned reading games, math games, phonics lessons, and interactive storybooks, the app has helped over 21 million preschool and elementary students learn at home, at school, and on the go. Join Kodi the Bear and friends on exciting educational adventures that spark curiosity, build confidence, and inspire a lifelong love of learning. PLAY-BASED READING, MATH & MORE: From ABC games and phonics practice to counting, addition, and shapes, kids can explore over 5,000 educational games and activities with Kodi’s friends: • Ollo the Elephant – phonics and letter sounds • Reya the Red Panda – storytime and writing • Peck the Hummingbird – numbers and counting • Sandy the Dingo – puzzles, memory, and problem-solving AWARDS AND RECOGNITION: With more than 180,000 5-star reviews, Khan Academy Kids has won the hearts of families and educators worldwide. • “Best kids app EVER” • “It’s 100% free and my kids learn so much!” • “If you’re looking for a HIGH quality app for your kids, this is it!” Recognition includes: • Common Sense Media – Top Rated Educational App • Children’s Technology Review – Editor’s Choice • Parents’ Choice – Gold Award Winner • Apple App Store – Editor’s Choice A LIBRARY OF STORYBOOKS AND VIDEOS: • Discover hundreds of kids’ books and videos for preschool, kindergarten and early elementary. • Explore animals, dinosaurs, science, and more with non-fiction books from National Geographic and Bellwether Media. • Choose “Read To Me” for read-aloud storybooks in English or Spanish. • Dance and sing-along with videos from Super Simple Songs! FROM PRESCHOOL TO 2ND GRADE: Khan Academy Kids grows with your child, from age 2 through 8 and beyond: • Preschool learning games build foundational reading, math, and life skills. • Kindergarten activities cover phonics, sight words, writing, and early math. • 1st and 2nd grade lessons strengthen reading comprehension, problem-solving, and confidence. SAFE, TRUSTED, AND ALWAYS FREE: Created in partnership with the Stanford Graduate School of Education by education experts, aligned with Head Start and Common Core Standards, COPPA-compliant, and 100% free—no ads, no subscriptions. Khan Academy is a nonprofit with the mission to provide a free, world-class education for anyone, anywhere. LEARN ANYWHERE—AT HOME, AT SCHOOL, EVEN OFFLINE: • At home: Khan Academy Kids is the perfect learning app for families at home. From sleepy mornings to road trips, kids and families love learning with Khan Kids. For homeschool: Families that homeschool also enjoy our standards-aligned, educational kids games and lessons for kids. • At school: In-app Teacher Tools help preschool and elementary school teachers create assignments, track student progress, and make the most of small-group and whole-group learning. • On the go: No wifi? No problem! Download books and games for learning on the go. Perfect for car trips, waiting rooms, or cozy mornings at home. START YOUR LEARNING ADVENTURE TODAY Download Khan Academy Kids and watch your child discover, play, and grow. JOIN OUR COMMUNITIES FOR FAMILIES AND TEACHERS Follow @khankids on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. KHAN ACADEMY: Khan Academy is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization with the mission to provide a free, world-class education to anyone, anywhere. What is Khan Academy Kids? 

A free educational app for children ages 2–8, with games, books, and lessons that build early literacy, math, and social-emotional skills.

![Image 26](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/687556c5aa293822fea47666/6a26e5de87d798c8d72c6cba_ic_fluent_chevron_right_24_filled.png)

Is Khan Academy Kids really free?

Yes — the mobile app is 100% free, with no ads or subscriptions. For schools and districts using Khan Academy Kids across multiple classrooms, we recommend [Khan Academy Kids for Schools](https://www.khanacademy.org/kids/schools-districts). 

![Image 27](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/687556c5aa293822fea47666/6a26e5de87d798c8d72c6cba_ic_fluent_chevron_right_24_filled.png)

Who is it for?

The free Khan Academy Kids mobile app is for families with children ages 2–8, and for teachers or homeschool families supporting children in PreK–2nd grade. For Schools and Districts, we suggest exploring [Khan Academy Kids for Schools](https://www.khanacademy.org/kids/schools-districts). 

![Image 28](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/687556c5aa293822fea47666/6a26e5de87d798c8d72c6cba_ic_fluent_chevron_right_24_filled.png)

Is there a version for schools and districts?

Yes — for schools and districts implementing across multiple classrooms, we recommend Khan Academy Kids for Schools. For $5 per student, you get features that make implementing at scale easy: a web-based dashboard for teachers and administrators, school- and district-level reporting, professional development, and ongoing support.

![Image 29](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/687556c5aa293822fea47666/6a26e5de87d798c8d72c6cba_ic_fluent_chevron_right_24_filled.png)

Has Khan Academy Kids won any awards?

Yes. Khan Academy Kids is 5-star rated by Common Sense Media, and has received Editor's Choice recognition from Children's Technology Review, a Gold Award from Parents' Choice, and Editors' Choice recognition on the Apple App Store.

![Image 30](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/687556c5aa293822fea47666/6a26e5de87d798c8d72c6cba_ic_fluent_chevron_right_24_filled.png)

Is Khan Academy Kids backed by research?

Yes. The app is developed with early learning experts and has been independently studied, including a peer-reviewed UMass Amherst trial showing pre-literacy gains for participating preschoolers. 

![Image 31](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/687556c5aa293822fea47666/6a26e5de87d798c8d72c6cba_ic_fluent_chevron_right_24_filled.png)

What happens to my child's information?

Khan Academy Kids comes from Khan Academy, a nonprofit. There's no advertising business behind the app and no reason to monetize your family's information.  

*   We don't sell personal information.
*   We don't show ads in the app, and we don't let third parties track your child across other apps or websites.
*   We collect as little as we can. We ask for a name and age at setup, and we recommend using a nickname. We never ask your child for personal information directly.

# What is Khan Academy?

## What parents need to know

Khan Academy is an educational platform. It helps students learn about a range of topics using video lessons and quizzes.

![Khan Academy logo](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Khan-Academy-feature-300x158.webp)

## In this guide

## What is Khan Academy?

Khan Academy is an online learning resource that lets users learn about various topics by watching short videos and completing quizzes, which the user can do at their own pace. Khan Academy offers subjects like Maths, Computing, and Science..

The Khan Academy app is available on Android and iOS and is also available through internet browsers. All courses and lessons at Khan Academy are free. An app designed specifically for children aged 2-8 also exists called [Khan Academy Kids](https://learn.khanacademy.org/khan-academy-kids/).

## How it works

To start using Khan Academy, you must sign up and select a course that you’d like to take. Once you enroll in your course, you will get access to video lessons and quizzes. The platform organises these into groups called units.

These units are sequential, meaning that as you complete each unit, you will learn enough to be able to understand the next unit. However, if you already know the information in a particular unit, you can skip ahead to the next one without having to complete the ones preceding it.

Khan Academy has a gamified approach to learning, [similar to other skill-building apps like Duolingo](/advice/apps-and-platforms/skills-building/duolingo/), with users receiving points and badges for watching videos and completing quizzes. Receiving points can allow users to ‘evolve’ their Khan Academy avatar, getting a different version of their profile’s avatar. This can motivate children to stick with Khan Academy and complete lessons regularly.

Khan Academy has a community forum, where users can ask each other questions and get advice on the subjects they are studying. This forum is based heavily around education and the Khan Academy platform. Because of this, it is unlikely that users will be exposed to any inappropriate or upsetting content while using it.

There is a range of educational subjects that can be studied, such as Maths, Science and Economics, but Khan Academy also offers Life skills courses. These units include lessons on Internet Safety, Financial and Social Media Literacy, and how AI can be used in education. These options make Khan Academy a beneficial app for children even if they don’t use it for school subjects.

![A few people holding their devices with a logo inside it representing Internet Matters' artificial intelligence assistant. Text reads: Ask Internet Matters](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/hero-ask-internet-matters-300x158.webp)

### Need a quick answer?

Ask our AI assistant about devices, apps and games.

## Khan Academy parental controls

Khan Academy is an educational platform, with content that is appropriate for all ages. However, there is still an option to create a parent account and monitor your child’s activity.

To do this, parents must create a parent account and then send an invite to their child’s account. Once the child accepts the invitation, the parent will be able to view their activity on Khan Academy. However, this is purely a monitoring role, as parents cannot set any controls on their child’s account.

Being able to monitor activity will let parents stay aware of how much studying their child is doing, and it also lets them know what courses they are undertaking. With Khan Academy having lessons intended for all ages, from primary school to university students, this feature will mean parents are aware if their 8-year-old child is mistakenly signed up to a university economics course.

If you have a child younger than 8-years-old, you can create an account for them on Khan Academy Kids rather than regular Khan Academy. This app only has content meant for children and is more engaging for younger audiences. Animal characters guide children, and lessons use interactive activities like games and books. Using this app will also mean your child can’t access the community features of Khan Academy.

The Kid’s app does include parental controls. Because the app targets children, developers did not need to add many controls. The only settings parents can change are visual ones such as having seasonal themes.

![Digital Matters logo on white background.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/digital-matters-logo-300x158.webp)

### Free digital literacy lessons

Explore lessons at Digital Matters.

## Benefits of Khan Academy

## What to watch out for

Being an educational platform, there is very little risk of exposure to inappropriate or disturbing content while using Khan Academy. Moderation is strict on the community forum. They use AI to quickly remove any comments with bad language.

However, on any platform with community comments there is a chance that something will slip through the cracks, so your child should be prepared to see mean or inappropriate comments if they use the Khan Community forum. You can use our [Digital Resilience toolkit](https://www.internetmatters.org/resources/digital-resilience-toolkit/) to support your child and help them be less effected if they see this kind of content online.

Khan Academy is a US organisation, and therefore its courses are based heavily around the US education system. This can make some lessons, such as the ones based around college admissions, unhelpful for UK children. Explain to your child that this is an American app before they use it. This will help them understand any differences between the American and UK education systems.

Khan Academy can greatly benefit UK children who use it, regardless of their age.

# Is Khan Academy Kids a good fit for Your Child? An In-depth, No-Nonsense Review

[All In One](/all-resources/category/All+In+One)

Written By [Manisha Snoyer (CEO and co-founder of Modulo)](/all-resources?author=5d7ab498c194df04021d0c43)

*Updated on July 10, 2023*

*This review was written by* [*Manisha Snoyer*](https://www.linkedin.com/in/manisha-snoyer-5042298/)*, the founder and CEO of* [*Modulo*](https://modulo.app)*, a company that provides resources and support families who are homeschooling their children. With over 20 years of experience as a teacher, Manisha has instructed over 2,000 children of all ages and abilities in three countries and 18 subjects. She has tutored at some of the best private schools in the world and throughout the NYC public school system. Manisha graduated summa cum laude from Brandeis University.*

[![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5d7abe08c531b24d41f3386e/4ad62542-596a-4052-96a7-d27cef686e7c/Khan+Academy+Kids.png)](https://learn.khanacademy.org/khan-academy-kids/)

Unleash the power of the digital revolution in childhood education with Khan Academy Kids, a game-changer in the world of e-learning. Covering PreK-2nd grade, this app offers an unparalleled, personalized learning experience, right from the comforts of your home.

During the pandemic, we reviewed thousands of comments from parents, and spent over 10,000 hours testing [the top educational apps](https://joinmodulo.substack.com/p/50-educational-apps-your-kids-will) with our own students. Khan Academy Kids was our clear favorite for a free, personalized learning app covering all subjects for kids in PreK-2nd.

Developed as a sibling of the groundbreaking Khan Academy's website, Khan Academy Kids has cracked the code to make learning accessible and entertaining for children. While the conventional learning methods may not resonate with every child, Khan Academy Kids crafts lessons that adapt to your child's unique learning style.

Ideal for the tech-savvy generation, this app allows children to explore almost any subject, making learning a fun, self-paced adventure. As an answer to every parent's quest for an engaging educational tool, Khan Academy Kids stands out as a favorite among homeschooling families and educators alike.

**Cost:** Free!

**Grades:** PreK-2nd

## Key features of Khan Academy Kids

**Educational Content:** Khan Academy Kids offers a wide range of educational activities, games, and lessons covering various subjects, including math, reading, writing, language arts, social-emotional learning, and more. The content is specifically designed to align with early learning standards.

**Engaging Interface:** The platform presents content in a colorful and interactive format, with engaging characters and animations that help children stay interested and motivated.

**Personalized Learning**: Khan Academy Kids adapts to each child's learning level and pace. It offers personalized recommendations based on a child's progress and provides targeted exercises to address specific areas of improvement.

**Offline Learning:** The app includes offline activities, allowing children to continue learning even without an internet connection. This feature can be especially useful for families with limited internet access or during travel.

**Parental Controls:** Parents or guardians can create accounts and customize the learning experience for their children. They can track their child's progress, set time limits, and access additional resources to support their child's learning journey.

**Accessibility Features**: Khan Academy Kids is designed to be inclusive and offers accessibility features such as audio support, visual aids, and a user-friendly interface that accommodates children with different learning needs.

## Pros of Khan Academy Kids

**Inclusive and accessible:** Khan Academy Kids is designed to be inclusive and accessible to a wide range of learners. The app incorporates features such as audio support, visual aids, and a user-friendly interface

**Mastery-based Learning**: Let your child conquer a topic before proceeding to the next. The app's progressive learning model ensures thorough understanding, leading to accelerated learning.

**Incentivized Learning**: With colorful characters and captivating stories, the app motivates children to reach educational milestones, rewarding their achievements along the way.

**Customizable Curriculum:** Whether your child is gifted or has special learning needs, the app personalizes lessons, ensuring every child learns at their own pace.

**Comprehensive Tracking:** Parents, breathe easy! With built-in assessment tools, monitor your child's progress, measure their performance, and track their academic growth.

**Limitless Learning, Zero Cost:** Get access to unlimited subjects at no cost. Whether it's brushing up rusty physics concepts or supplementing regular learning, Khan Academy Kids is your go-to resource.

## Cons of Khan Academy Kids

**Screen time:** We understand **screen time** is a concern for many. We always encourage parents to play the app with their child, engage and ask questions, rather than using it as a form of passive entertainment. Different children respond different to screen time. Try to assess your child’s individual child’s needs and cultivate a healthy digital lifestyle for their children, balancing learning with other activities.

**Math program is underwhelming:** While the app offers a comprehensive curriculum, some feel **the math program could be more extensive**. Also, mastery-based learning might not suit all children, with some finding the pace too slow.

**Too test-oriented:** Moreover, some users find the app's **approach to testing predictable**, leading to success in tests without a complete understanding of the subject.

**Too traditional:** The app is designed to support children in having success at school, so some might find it too traditional and aligned with requirements for standardized testing.

**Not for kinesthetic learners:** As with all tools, **Khan Academy Kids may not be ideal for every child**, especially those who are **kinesthetic or have sensory challenges.** It is important to understand your child's learning style before choosing an educational platform.

## Homeschooling with Khan Academy Kids

Khan Academy Kids can be a great full curriculum, supplemented with a strong math curriculum for homeschooling. Many parents find homeschooling is more efficient than learning in a group setting in a classroom, and so they’ve adopted a practice of “mastery hours” where they spend two hours a day is plenty to cover all academic subjects, especially for a younger student. We recommend spending two hours a day with a core curriculum and math supplement, and using the rest of the time for extracurriculars, free play, practical life and self-directed learning. Learn more about [mastery hours](https://joinmodulo.substack.com/p/mastery-hours) and see a sample [homeschool schedule for an elementary student](https://joinmodulo.substack.com/p/whats-a-typical-homeschool-day-look).

## Reviews from parents and educators

Check out what educators and parents have to say about their experience with Khan Academy Kids.

**A Speech-Language Pathologist said**: "I was so impressed with how comprehensive this app is... My daughter has shown so much growth in her ability to recognize and name letters and sounds."

**A parent shared:** "My son with autism... has learned all about opposites and is reading!... Thank you so much for this gift!"

**Another parent revealed**: "We Absolutely love this app for our 7 kids that we homeschool! All the kids... love it especially for homeschooling."

## Frequently Asked Questions about Khan Academy Kids

## 1. What is the youngest age for Khan Academy?

Khan Academy offers resources and educational content for learners of all ages. While the main Khan Academy website primarily caters to middle school, high school, and college-level students, they have a separate platform called "Khan Academy Kids" that is specifically designed for children aged 2 to 7 years old.

## 2. Is Khan Academy age-appropriate?

Khan Academy provides age-appropriate educational content for different age groups. The main Khan Academy website covers a wide range of subjects and is primarily aimed at older students, while Khan Academy Kids is specifically tailored to the needs of children aged 2 to 7. The content and activities in Khan Academy Kids are designed to be engaging and suitable for early learners.

## 3. Does Khan Academy have Pre-K?

Khan Academy does not have a dedicated Pre-K program on its main website. However, they offer Khan Academy Kids, which provides educational resources and activities suitable for children as young as 2 years old. Khan Academy Kids is designed to support early learning and development in various subjects.

## 4. What is the best learning app for a 7-year-old?

The "best" learning app for a 7-year-old can vary depending on the child's interests and learning style. However, some popular learning apps for 7-year-olds include [Brain Pop Jr](https://joinmodulo.substack.com/i/121780633/brainpop-and-brain-pop-jr), [Epic!,](https://www.modulo.app/all-resources/getepic) [Prodigy Math Game](https://modulo.app/all-resources/prodigymathgame), [Math Tango](https://joinmodulo.substack.com/i/108596390/math-tango-k-th), [Toca Boca,](https://joinmodulo.substack.com/i/121780633/grades-all) and of course, Khan Academy Kids. It's recommended to explore different apps, consider the child's individual needs, and read reviews to determine the most suitable option. See our post [50 Educational Apps Your Kids Will Love](https://joinmodulo.substack.com/p/50-educational-apps-your-kids-will) for more guidance on choosing educational apps.

## 5. Is Khan Academy Kids free?

Yes, Khan Academy Kids is a free educational app available for download on mobile devices. It does not require a subscription or payment to access its content. However, please note that this information is accurate as of my knowledge cutoff in September 2021, and there may have been changes to Khan Academy Kids' pricing or features since then.

## 6. Where should a 7-year-old be academically?

Academic progress can vary among 7-year-olds, as each child develops at their own pace. Generally, a 7-year-old should be acquiring fundamental reading and writing skills, have basic numeracy abilities, and demonstrate age-appropriate social and emotional development. They may be learning about more complex math concepts, expanding their vocabulary, developing stronger reading comprehension skills, and exploring various subjects in school.

## 7. How can I help my 7-year-old learn?

There are several ways you can support your 7-year-old's learning:

- Encourage reading by providing age-appropriate books and reading together.

- Help with homework assignments and provide guidance when needed.

- Engage in conversations about their interests and encourage their curiosity.

- Provide opportunities for hands-on learning experiences and experiments.

- Support their organizational skills and establish a routine for studying and completing tasks.

- Communicate with their teachers to stay informed about their progress and areas of focus.

## 8. Should a 7-year-old be in 1st grade?

In many educational systems, 7-year-olds are typically in 1st or 2nd grade. However, educational structures can vary across different countries and school systems. It's best to refer to your specific educational system's guidelines or consult with teachers or school administrators to determine the appropriate grade level for a 7-year-old.

## 9. Why is my 7-year-old being so difficult?

There can be various reasons why a 7-year-old might display challenging behavior. Children at this age are undergoing significant cognitive and emotional development, which can lead to changes in behavior. Some possible reasons for difficult behavior could include frustration, lack of emotional regulation skills, difficulties with transitions or changes, environmental factors, or underlying emotional or developmental issues. It's important to approach difficult behavior with patience, understanding, and open communication. If the challenging behavior persists or significantly affects the child's well-being, it may be helpful to seek guidance from a pediatrician, psychologist, or other child development professionals.

### 10. How can I improve my 7 year old’s social skills?

Khan Academy Kids incorporates elements of social-emotional learning into its content to support the development of social skills in young children. While the primary focus of Khan Academy Kids is on early literacy, math, and other academic subjects, the platform also integrates activities and stories that promote social-emotional growth. These activities may include teaching empathy, understanding emotions, problem-solving, and cooperation. Through engaging stories, interactive games, and characters, Khan Academy Kids aims to foster the social and emotional development of young learners. To improve your 7-year-old's social skills, encourage playdates with peers to foster interaction and cooperation. Engage in role-playing activities to practice social scenarios, teaching empathy and problem-solving. Lead by example and exhibit positive social behavior in your own interactions. Teach active listening and effective communication techniques. Encourage participation in clubs or activities aligned with their interests to promote social connections. Emphasize respect, kindness, and inclusivity towards others. Create an open environment for communication and seek professional help if needed. With patience and consistent support, your child can develop essential social skills that will benefit them throughout their lives.
